body:
Use the [published vLLM release](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20261113-0ac9dcb157ee) at `0ac9dcb157ee` for standalone GPU serving with Torch 2.14.1 and CUDA 13.2.2. It includes Hero version 3 query scaling and fixes for BF16 RMSNorm rounding, stale FP8 padding scales and missing ShortConv decode outputs. The GPU launcher installs this stack in its isolated serving environment. Trainer adoption stays in #11307; TPU adoption stays in #11285.

The x86_64 and aarch64 wheels passed the [H100 and GB200 release gates](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/actions/runs/43379837147). Fresh Snowball checks passed 64 prompts each at one and two pipeline stages, with compilation and CUDA graphs enabled. Maximum token-probability errors were 0.124960 and 0.124768, respectively, against the unchanged 0.125 bound. Both results are close to the acceptance bound.

The affected CPU suite has 1,000 passes, nine failures and one collection skip. The nine failures match the independent main `200c32d` baseline: missing Python pidfd support, hash fixtures and a NixOS shell-path assumption. Required lint passes; advisory review has no findings. Rollback restores `marin-vllm-gpu-20260924-01911be34fac` and its generated pins.
title: Adopt vLLM 0ac9dcb for standalone GPU serving
